frozen: Written and committed before any run, after readings.py, the router change and the scoring change were written. The phrasings were written without running the two-reading rule on them. Run once; not edited after it has been run. Its first result stands as reported.
purpose: Questions with two plain readings (distinct patients, or each admission, visit, discharge or readmission), beside questions whose wording settles the unit. Measures whether Agere gives both readings when they differ, answers once when they agree, and does not ask on questions that have one reading.
held_out: Not used by the learning loop, the curriculum or as recipe examples. The stack is scored on a copy of its saved recipes with learning switched off.
reference: Computed in clinical_core/agere/tiered/proof.py on the semantic layer by independent Python: the event readings are the existing references (stays merged into hospital episodes, ED visits by the governed hospital_visit rule); the patient readings are the distinct patients of the same events (ref_rd_*).
phrasing: Two phrasings each, both in everyday wording.
scoring: +1 right, 0 declined, -10 wrong; an unanswerable question that is answered counts as wrong. A question with two readings ('readings') scores +1 when both readings are given and each is right, 0 when one figure is given and it matches one of the readings, -10 otherwise; where the two readings give the same number, one right answer is +1. Asking on a question with one reading scores 0. Arms: stack (with the two-reading check), stack_guess (the same stack answering one reading, as before) and frontier. Two runs, all reported.
